jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: The State of Palestine steers AI through strategy and policy led by the Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Economy (MTDE); there is no AI-specific law and no personal data protection law in force. A national AI team formed by the Council of Ministers in 2021 under MTDE prepared a National AI Strategy and National AI Policy (2023), whose adoption is stated in MTDE documents. The AI commitments set out in official documents are in MTDE's Digital Government Strategy 2024-2029 (AI infrastructure, skills and pilot AI services in government), the Ministry Strategy 2025-2027 (AI as a strategic priority and an update of the AI strategy with legal and ethical frameworks) and the General Policy for the Telecom and IT Sectors 2026-2028 (AI regulatory, ethics and transparency frameworks, especially for government AI). The direction is towards an updated AI strategy, AI governance and ethics frameworks, and a pending data protection decree-law.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Economy (MTDE)
narrative.review_notes: Not yet verified from the official text: the National AI Strategy and National AI Policy (2023), expected on the national AI portal ai.gov.ps, the National AI Ethics Charter and the 2021 Council of Ministers decision forming the national AI team. The electronic-transactions and cybercrime decree-laws contain no AI provisions. Not yet verified from the official text: the official gazette, the cabinet, the standards institution and the Palestine Monetary Authority's legislation pages.

Prepared by the then Ministry of Telecom and IT with Cambridge consultants under the World Bank-funded Digital West Bank & Gaza project.
instruments.summary: Palestine's digital-government strategy for 2024-2029, prepared by the Ministry of Telecommunications and IT with stakeholders. Its innovation objective (activity 4.8) commits the ministry to build government infrastructure for AI and big data, train civil servants in AI and data analytics, pilot AI applications in government services (e.g. security monitoring, smart health care) and run public awareness on the benefits and risks of AI. It lists ISO/IEC 23053 (framework for AI systems using machine learning) among the international standards recommended for government systems.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Strategy with an explicit AI pillar for government use of AI; guides ministries, not binding.

instruments.summary: The ministry's three-year strategy for telecoms, IT, the digital economy and post. "Enhancing artificial intelligence" is one of its eleven strategic priorities, and it notes that the AI sector has developed following the launch of the national AI strategy and national AI policy. It commits the ministry to update the national AI strategy so as to set the legal, ethical and regulatory frameworks needed to deploy AI in the public and private sectors, prioritising AI use in government services, institutional efficiency, capacity building and research.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Ministry strategy that names AI as a strategic priority and commits to an updated AI strategy with legal and ethical frameworks; not binding.

instruments.summary: Sector policy issued by the Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Economy for 2026-2028 in two parts (telecoms and IT). In the IT part the State commits to develop comprehensive regulatory frameworks for emerging technologies including AI, IoT and cloud, setting ethical, security and operational safeguards, and to encourage national frameworks for the governance and ethics of AI that ensure transparency and non-discrimination, especially in AI used in government services. It also ties data governance to responsible AI and refers to the pending draft data protection law and cybersecurity law.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Policy commitment to an AI regulatory and ethics framework, particularly for government AI; not binding until approved.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Official sources and each national ministry were searched for laws, data protection, cybersecurity, procurement, transparency, sandboxes, sectoral rules (the monetary authority, education, health and telecoms), generative AI and standards, and no qualifying AI-governance document was found in these categories. The national AI strategy, policy and ethics charter exist and are listed as leads to check later, together with a draft data protection law. Regional instruments (UNESCO) apply through the regional section.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Method note (original): Deep review completed on 7 October 2026. The national AI portal, which holds the 2023 AI strategy and policy, could not be reached, so both are pending. The official gazette, the cabinet, the standards institution and the Palestine Monetary Authority's legislation pages could not be read. The electronic-transactions and cybercrime decree-laws were reviewed and contain no AI provisions. No government action with a confirmed exact date was found, so no dated events are recorded.

Coverage note (original): Searched, nothing found on an official source: no AI-specific law or general law with AI provisions (e-transactions, trust services and cybercrime decree-laws checked); no data protection law in force (draft only, a lead); no AI cybersecurity, procurement, transparency, sandbox, sectoral (PMA, education, health, telecom) or generative-AI guidance; no PSI adoption of AI standards found (PSI site unreachable). The national AI strategy, policy and ethics charter exist but their texts on ai.gov.ps could not be read, so they are leads. Regional instruments (UNESCO) apply via data/regional. Technical review notes: Deep review 2026-10-07. ai.gov.ps (national AI portal holding the AI strategy and policy) fails TLS (self-signed certificate) and returns 503, so those documents are leads. The Official Gazette reference (mjr.ogb.gov.ps) is behind a Cloudflare challenge; dft.gov.ps, palestinecabinet.gov.ps, psi.gov.ps and muqtafi.birzeit.edu were unreachable through the proxy. pma.ps is a JavaScript single-page app whose legislation and fintech pages could not be read; the PMA fintech regulatory sandbox (launched 2022) is a general fintech sandbox with no AI-specific scope found, so it is not recorded. The old MTIT site (mtit.gov.ps) holds only pre-2021 documents with no AI content. Decree-Law 15/2017 on electronic transactions, Decree-Law 10/2018 on cybercrime and the later decree-law on electronic transactions and trust services were checked and excluded: they contain no AI provisions. The National Blockchain Policy 2026-2028 (MTDE) mentions AI once and is out of scope. Excluded university AI policies (not government). No precise-dated government action was confirmed on an official source, so no world events were added. Ministry catch-up 2026-10-13 (PROTOCOL §2 ministry rule, applied after this country's deep review; one agent, 30 minutes, national ministries' own AI documents only, nothing else re-reviewed): 0 record(s) added. Ministries: Ministry of Education and Higher Education (schools): Education Development Strategy 2025-2027 and governing laws/instructions checked, nothing found; Ministry of Education and Higher Education (higher education/research): Higher Education Sector Strategy 2025-2027 has AI activities only (lead), National Centre for Emerging Technologies and AI founding instrument not found (lead), ministerial regulations/decisions list has no AI item; Ministry of Health: national site (moh.ps) unreachable; Gaza-based moh.gov.ps has only AI news items, nothing found; Justice: Ministry of Justice and Public Prosecution sites unreachable, Supreme Judicial Council site read (digital-transformation 'Mizan 3' news only), nothing found; Defence: no defence ministry (security services under Interior), nothing found; Finance/tax/customs: Ministry of Finance site unreachable, searches found nothing; Interior/police/security: national site unreachable, searches found only academic work, nothing found; Foreign Affairs: site unreachable, nothing found; Labour/employment: site unreachable, nothing found; Social Development: strategy checked, nothing found; Agriculture: Strategy 2025-2027 checked, nothing found; National Economy/trade: site unreachable, nothing found; Transport, Energy (PENRA), Environment, Public Works, Tourism, Culture, Local Government: nothing found (culture, local government and tourism sites scanned; others unreachable); Public administration/civil service (General Personnel Council): site unreachable, no public-servant AI guidance found; Telecommunications and Digital Economy: already recorded (3 records, 6 leads), no further ministry document found. Not reached: moh.ps (Ministry of Health, Ramallah) - unreachable; moj.pna.ps (Ministry of Justice) - unreachable; pgp.ps (Public Prosecution) - unreachable; pmof.ps (Ministry of Finance) - unreachable (503); moi.pna.ps (Ministry of Interior, Ramallah) - unreachable; mofa.pna.ps (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) - unreachable (503); mol.pna.ps (Ministry of Labour) - unreachable (503); gpc.pna.ps (General Personnel Council) - unreachable (503); mne.pna.ps (Ministry of National Economy) - unreachable; palestinecabinet.gov.ps (Council of Ministers) - unreachable; aqac (Accreditation and Quality Assurance Commission) - unreachable. Could not verify: Health, Justice, Public Prosecution, Finance, Interior, Foreign Affairs, Labour, National Economy, General Personnel Council and Cabinet sites could not be reached with curl or WebFetch, so their own pages could not be checked directly; searches found no AI documents from them.; National Centre for Emerging Technologies and AI: founding decision, date and issuer unverified..
